title: Don't Fail to Come: How Burroughs Talked Wellcome Into London
conflicts: Partnership capital: Beckett (2008), quoting Rhodes James, gives £2,000 split £1,200/£800 but says Wellcome paid only £400 cash and borrowed £550 at 10%, which does not add up; the story says only that Burroughs lent him much of his share at ten per cent. Ages differ (Wellcome 26 or 27; Grace's Guide gives Burroughs 35, though born December 1846), so no ages are given. Hoffman (1995) calls the firm 'incorporated' and an 'instant success'; Church (2005) describes a partnership and slow persuasion, so Hoffman's claims are not used. A 2013 Sudan J Paediatr article misdates Burroughs's death to 1885 and was excluded. Outcome numbers: Church's hedged first-year sales ('may have reached £2,000') not used; only his 600 employees by 1892 is given, attributed.
notes: The episode is told as the founding decision: Burroughs's 1879-80 letters inviting Wellcome (quoted from Church's Medical History article, which draws on the Wellcome archive) and Wellcome's hesitation (Hoffman). Ends with the 1889 failed dissolution suit and Burroughs's death in 1895. PubMed Central loaded and named the founders on the first check but later served a page the checker could not read (NO-NAME); the edition still passes on the other four sources.
